purpose: Every quantitative VLM/VSPAERO claim Liming Zheng (DSO) has made about ARGUS morphing-candidate performance, each with its operating point and normalising frame attached, and each marked current / superseded / withdrawn.
reading_rules: NO percentage or drag count in this file may be quoted without the operating_point_id AND the frame_id that sit beside it.
Liming's reports supersede each other. Only entries with status=current are quotable as present DSO results.
Liming never quotes total drag. Every claim below is induced drag only: near-field CDi or wake/Trefftz CDiw. See notes.induced_drag_only.
A percentage reduction is invariant to Sref because baseline and candidate share it. A DRAG COUNT IS NOT. See frames.collision.

method.solver: VSPAERO (vortex lattice) driven through the OpenVSP Python API
method.objective_current: min CDiw (wake / Trefftz-plane induced drag) only. Was min CDi (surface-integration) before 2026-08-19.

optimiser.surrogate: Gaussian-process regression, Matern-5/2 kernel, normalised design variables; separate models for the drag objective and for the root-bending metric
optimiser.acquisition: S(x) = CDi_hat(x) - lambda_sigma * sigma_hat(x) + P_constraints(x) + P_distance(x)
optimiser.inner_search_lowspeed: differential evolution, population-size factor 12, <=60 surrogate-only inner iterations, polishing, batch size 4
optimiser.inner_search_cruise: 200000 smooth random schedules screened per batch with the GP; 4 role-specific geometries retained (early min, early constraint boundary, late min, late uncertainty exploration)
optimiser.stopping_rule: prescribed budget of adaptive batches, not a convergence proof
optimiser.reported_values: ALWAYS exact VSPAERO reruns with strict iterative fixed-lift trim. The surrogate only chooses where to evaluate.

trailing_edge_camber.interpolation_cruise: shape-preserving piecewise cubic; tip value free (the earlier parameterisation forced it to zero and made an artificial tip discontinuity)

distributed_twist.kinematics: whole local section rotates, airfoil profile preserved

conventional_hinged.bound_rationale: equal maximum trailing-edge displacement to the continuous concept: |dz_TE/c|max = 0.035, |delta|max = asin(0.035/(1-0.70)) = 6.65 deg. The physical NASA TP-1580 mechanical range is about +/-30 deg but that is for control, not cruise adaptation.
conventional_hinged.representation: zero-gap outer-mold-line approximation; no hinge gap, seal, bracket or leakage modelled

design_variables.morphing_region: 0.60 <= eta <= 1.00 for both continuous concepts (the earliest twist DOE and the rotation-axis study used 0.60 <= eta <= 0.95)

lowspeed: max adjacent command |Ai/c - Ai-1/c| <= 0.018 with virtual A0 = A6 = 0 (illustrative numerical smoothness screen)
cruise: absolute half-wing root bending Mroot <= Mlim = 2.9266 MNm, set equal to the rigid early-cruise value, illustrative not certified
m01_cl0529_historical: Mroot <= Mroot_rigid = 180.115 kN m, no positive feasibility tolerance
constraints.withdrawn: the 1050 N m hinge-torque proxy limit, disabled in code, neither fitted nor penalised

trim.fast: small alpha sweep, local lift-curve slope, one load case near the target, used inside the optimisation loop only
trim.strict: iterative fixed-lift trim, tolerance |CL - CL_target| <= 2e-5; this is what every reported number uses

lowspeed_historical_125.note: count breakdown is the 19 Aug post-dedup audit; the 29 Jul report stated 40/22/22 for the first 85-case pass plus 2x20 local refinements

evaluation_counts.conventional_cruise_search: 5x5 exact grid over [-6.65, 6.65]^2 then 8 extra points; 33 geometries, 66 strict evaluations; no surrogate used (only 2 design variables)

surrogate_quality_cross_validation.note: five-fold CV of the stage-one cruise models
surrogate_quality_cross_validation.liming_caveat: the weak trailing-edge drag surrogate is an important limitation; selected TE cases are best exact SAMPLED candidates, not proven global optima

geometry_generation.baseline: public NASA-style OpenVSP EET cruise wing, wing-only (fuselage, tail, slats, high-lift removed)
geometry_generation.refinement: 10 spanwise sections inserted, mainly 0.55 <= eta <= 0.95, section count 9 -> 19
geometry_generation.inserted_airfoil_method_corrected: both bracketing airfoils resampled onto a common cosine-spaced x/c grid then linearly blended in eta; max coordinate error 3.71e-12 c; MAC change 5.21e-7 ft

supersessions.what: The 1050 N m 'hinge-torque proxy' limit, the resulting 99.98 % utilisation figure, the legacy feasible/infeasible Boolean for mbr_c01_l011, and every three- and four-actuator stroke/segment-lift/torque table derived from it.
supersessions.why: Two defects. (1) The quantity was a moment about the GLOBAL AIRCRAFT REFERENCE POINT, formed by shifting the VSPAERO sectional cmy to an assumed quarter chord, NOT a moment about the local xh/c = 0.62 hinge line. (2) The 1050 value was an illustrative internal optimisation bound with no traceable actuator specification.
supersessions.consequence: The optimiser may have rejected otherwise useful camber candidates against a non-physical constraint. The constraint is now disabled in code and is neither fitted nor penalised.
supersessions.still_valid: Dimensionless CL, CD, CDi remain valid for their archived geometries.
supersessions.replacement: H(eta) = integral over S(eta) of [(r - r_h) x (-p n)] . e_h dS, about the local xh/c = 0.62 line over 0.60 <= eta <= 1.00, unit / frame / sign convention / operating point stated explicitly. Positive trailing-edge down.

supersessions.what: All legacy post-processed absolute load/moment columns labelled N, N/m or Nm from the low-speed chain; TE_displacement_m as a metre-valued column (its stored values are FEET).
supersessions.why: Native OpenVSP Chord, dSpan and Yavg are in FEET and had been used as though metres.
supersessions.still_valid: Native .lod, .polar, .history, .vspaero files and their feet-based geometry fields. Dimensionless CL, CD, CDi, Cm. Relative root-bending PERCENTAGES, because baseline and candidate share the same geometry scale and condition so the error cancels.

supersessions.what: SplitWingXSec had copied ONE NEIGHBOURING airfoil-coordinate array into each inserted spanwise section instead of blending between the bracketing profiles. This changed the BASE SURFACE on which every subsequent morphing command was applied.
supersessions.found_by: independent CFD-ingest inspection on our side
supersessions.fix: Both bracketing airfoils resampled onto a common cosine-spaced x/c grid, then linearly blended in eta. Original sections retained untouched. Max coordinate error 3.71e-12 c; MAC change 5.21e-7 ft; span unchanged; area and AR differences at floating-point round-off.
supersessions.numerical_consequence: The rigid low-speed baseline CDi moved from 0.009167627 to 0.009878742, i.e. +7.76 %. Every pre-correction percentage is against a different reference wing.
supersessions.feasibility_consequence: The unchanged mcv2_i002_c01 command went from 6.646 % root-bending increase (feasible) to 7.124 % (INFEASIBLE against the illustrative 6.8 % screen). It was therefore demoted from 'audited constrained optimum' to 'RANS validation geometry'.

supersessions.what: Every induced-drag ranking, percentage and candidate selection was recomputed on the wake/Trefftz-plane coefficient CDiw instead of the surface-integration coefficient CDi.
supersessions.why: VSPAERO writes BOTH in each native .polar. The earlier pipeline extracted only CDi. A complete native-output audit concluded CDiw is the physically appropriate induced-drag quantity for the VLM/RANS comparison. Our independent lifting-line check supported it.
supersessions.scope: Not a relabelling. Every stored native polar had to be reparsed, every concept reranked, and new optimisation batches targeted CDiw directly (two dedicated four-case batches per continuous concept at both Mach numbers).
supersessions.audit_volume: 102 cruise geometries, 204 state evaluations, 816 native solver files. Max CL closure error 1.87e-5. Stored CSV CDi and CDiw match their native polar fields exactly. Recomputed span efficiency agrees with native Ew to 1.51e-7.
changed_orderings: Cruise EARLY: the CDi ranking put twist first (0.457 %) and trailing edge NEGATIVE (-0.121 %). The CDiw ranking puts trailing edge first (1.424 %) ahead of twist (1.031 %). THE WINNER CHANGED.
Cruise LATE: CDi gave TE 3.018 % and twist 1.767 %, a clear TE lead. CDiw gives TE 4.302 % and twist 4.313 %, a tie with twist marginally ahead.
Low speed 125-case at CL 0.529297: CDi gave twist 0.679 % ahead of TE 0.594 %. CDiw gives TE 0.596 % ahead of twist 0.423 %. THE WINNER CHANGED.
Low speed corrected at CL 0.428277635108: the TE-twist separation shrank from 0.664 drag counts (CDi) to 0.115 drag counts (CDiw).
supersessions.liming_instruction: 'All report statements that used near-field CDi as the optimized induced-drag metric are historical. Archived plots and case identifiers remain available for traceability, but they must not be mixed with the current far-field ranking.'

supersessions.was_2026-07-28_to_2026-08-10: 'Distributed twist should be carried forward as the primary high-authority concept because it performs best when the early-cruise bending constraint is active.'
supersessions.now_2026-08-19: 'Continuous trailing-edge camber is the current low-order aerodynamic benchmark: it gives the largest verified early-cruise reduction and is effectively tied with twist in late cruise.' Twist remains a serious candidate for its bidirectional authority, not for its induced drag.
supersessions.caution: Both statements are conditional on an ILLUSTRATIVE, uncertified root-bending allowable that both early-cruise candidates sit within 0.5 % of. Liming states a sensitivity sweep over 88-108 % of that limit can change the ordering again.

vlm_accuracy_and_limitation_statements.note: Liming's own words about what the method can and cannot support. These are the caveats that must travel with any DSO number quoted in our report.
on_the_method: 'VSPAERO is a low-order method; viscous effects, separation, detailed three-dimensional flow physics, and local pressure recovery are not fully resolved.'
'The current analysis should therefore be interpreted as a conceptual aerodynamic model rather than a high-fidelity CFD result.'
'VSPAERO does not resolve the Mach 0.78 shock/wave-drag physics.' (pkg_2026-08-07 README)
'At M = 0.78, the matched cruise comparison also cannot resolve transonic shock and wave-drag effects and therefore requires RANS validation.'
'The separate M = 0.1 fixed-CL study removes the transonic applicability concern but does not add viscous profile drag, hinge-gap loss, transition, separation, or actuator/structural penalties.'
on_the_conventional_benchmark: 'The conventional result must also be read as an optimistic aerodynamic reference. Its VSPAERO representation has no hinge gap, leakage, seal, bracket, transition, or profile-drag increment.'

'Conversely, the continuous concepts use more spanwise authority than the physical NASA aileron.' (NASA aileron 0.710 <= eta <= 0.970, x/c >= 0.70; ARGUS continuous concepts 0.60 <= eta <= 1.00) 'Consequently, this is a reference-concept comparison rather than an equal-area mechanism comparison.'
on_the_surrogate: 'Five-fold cross-validation gives R2 = 0.93-0.97 for the twist induced-drag models and R2 = 0.27-0.45 for the more difficult trailing-edge induced-drag models.'
'The trailing-edge CDi surrogate has moderate cross-validation quality, so the selected TE cases are best exact sampled candidates, not proven global optima.'
'The convergence plot is therefore evidence of diminishing improvement within that budget, not a proof of global convergence.'
'The search uses six adaptive batches for trailing-edge camber and four for twist ... and therefore still does not prove a global optimum.'
on_what_the_percentages_mean: 'All current percentage benefits in this section refer to wake/Trefftz induced drag CDiw, NOT total aircraft drag, fuel burn, or mission range. Viscous, wave, interference, actuator-mass, and structural-mass effects are outside this ranking.'
'The numbers should therefore be read as aerodynamic load-shaping evidence rather than a direct operating-cost prediction.'
'The M = 0.1 percentages must not be compared directly with the physical early/late-cruise percentages as if they represented the same flight state.'
'Earlier low-speed studies are retained to document method development; their percentages should not be compared directly with the physical early/late-cruise results.'
on_the_resolution_floor: 'Trailing-edge camber leads twist by only 0.115 drag counts, which is below the useful concept-separation capability of the planned matched-mesh RANS comparison.'
'Their 0.0108-percentage-point difference is too small to support an aerodynamic down-selection.' (late cruise)

'The trailing-edge/twist difference is only 0.115 drag count. It is too small for an aerodynamic hardware down-selection and is below the useful resolution of the matched-mesh RANS concept comparison.' (pkg_2026-08-19 README)
on_the_audit_itself: 'Passing the audit establishes internal reproducibility of the saved result chain; it is not an independent aerodynamic validation. The same OpenVSP baseline and VSPAERO method are used throughout the compared cases.'
'The pre-geometry-correction audit established arithmetic consistency but did NOT establish that the refined airfoil interpolation or induced-drag field was appropriate.'
on_the_structural_allowable: 'The limit is set equal to the rigid-wing early-cruise value. It is deliberately an illustrative design limit rather than a certified structural allowable.'
'Neither 6.8 % nor 0.018 is a certified structural or manufacturing allowable.' (pkg_2026-07-29)
'Wing fuel-weight relief is not included in the current net root-bending calculation.'
'The early-cruise result is simultaneously a statement about aerodynamic authority and about the chosen structural allowable.'
vlm_accuracy_and_limitation_statements.independent_cross_check_liming_ran: A Glauert/Fourier lifting-line calculation applied to the selected spanwise loadings. Reproduces unit span efficiency on an elliptical self-test and closes integrated CL to about 1e-6. Its absolute drag differs from VSPAERO because of modal truncation, but it supports the same low-speed ordering (TE lowest induced drag, twist close behind).

induced_drag_only.statement: NO Liming report quotes CDtot or CDo. Every performance claim in every version is CDi or CDiw, i.e. induced drag alone. Verified by grep across all five report texts: zero occurrences of CDtot, CDo or 'total drag' as a quoted result.
induced_drag_only.consequence: The RANS-versus-VLM comparison is induced drag against induced drag BY CONSTRUCTION on Liming's side. The usual trap (comparing VSPAERO CDtot, which contains a flat-plate skin-friction correlation CDo, against a real viscous RANS total drag) is not present in his claims.
induced_drag_only.but: The delivered native .polar files DO carry CDo and CDtot, and the delivered selected_cases_near_vs_far.csv carries a CD_total_near_field column. Those values are a FLAT-PLATE SKIN-FRICTION ESTIMATE, not a computed viscous solution, and must not be compared against RANS total drag.

near_field_vs_far_field_gap.statement: On the corrected low-speed baseline the near-field CDi is 0.009878741611 and the wake CDiw is 0.005667805449. The near-field value is 74.3 % higher than the far-field one on the same solver run.
near_field_vs_far_field_gap.span_efficiency: The same file gives near-field E = 0.548218049330 and wake Ew = 0.955520528139. A VLM wing at this loading should not have e = 0.55; the far-field value is the credible one, which is the physical argument behind S4.
near_field_vs_far_field_gap.consequence_for_us: Our RANS Trefftz-plane counterpart (resp_2026-09-02: four planes, e = 0.874 at the nearest plane x1) is the correct thing to compare against Ew = 0.9555, NOT against E = 0.5482.

what_liming_asks_from_us: Low-speed pressure-integrated LOCAL hinge moment about the swept xh/c = 0.62 line, projected on its local tangent, surfaces aft of the line only, over 0.60 <= eta <= 1.00, positive trailing-edge down. Pressure, viscous and total reported SEPARATELY, as sectional moment per unit span [N m/m], c_mh = m'_h/(q_inf c(y)^2), integrated half-wing moment [N m], and C_Mh,region = M_h/(q_inf * integral c(y)^2 dy).
Compressible / transonic validation on the ARGUS geometry.
A RANS counterpart to CDiw (Trefftz-plane induced drag).
Comparison of VSPAERO spanwise distributions against OpenFOAM/RANS strip loads BEFORE relying on the small TE-versus-twist difference.
A traceable structural allowable to replace the illustrative 6.8 % / 2.9266 MNm screens, including fuel-weight relief.
notes.liming_explicit_warning_on_low_speed_hin: 'Low-speed hinge moment must not be used directly for cruise actuator sizing.' (pkg_2026-08-19 README)

flags.title: The 19 August report's own prose misstates the low-speed reference area.
flags.detail: Report section 14.1 (line 3815) says 'The comparison uses the same NASA EET reference wing with the NASA Sref = 12 ft2, bref = 12 ft, and ARref = 12 convention', and section 13.2 (line 3327) repeats it. That is TRUE for the M = 0.78 cruise runs and FALSE for the M = 0.10 runs, whose native .vspaero decks all carry Sref = 13.3572, Cref = 1.29251.
flags.resolution: Believe the native decks, not the prose. Confirmed independently by the span-efficiency closure: ew recomputed on AR = 10.7807 matches the native low-speed Ew to 2.08e-07, and on AR = 12 it misses by 1.13e-01.
flags.action: Any DSO cruise coefficient or drag count we place beside a RANS number on the DSO basis (Sref 1.24092 m2) must be multiplied by 0.898392. Percentages need no conversion.

flags.title: Two different M = 0.1 operating points share a Mach number and a concept vocabulary.
flags.detail: op_m01_cl0428 (CL 0.428277635108, current, corrected geometry) and op_m01_cl0529 (CL 0.529297, historical 125-case, pre-correction geometry). Liming's own exec summary moves between them within a paragraph. The CL 0.529297 value was chosen only because it equals the early-cruise target.
flags.action: State the CL inline every time a low-speed DSO percentage is quoted. This is D076 inside the DSO deliveries.

flags.title: The number the task brief quoted is superseded.
flags.detail: 'reduce CDi by 4.567%, 6.524%, and 5.851%' is the 29 July / 7 August / 10 August corrected low-speed CDi result at M 0.1, CL 0.428277635108. The current equivalent is CDiw 0.520 %, 1.705 %, 1.502 % on different selected geometries. Quoting 6.524 % as current would overstate the trailing-edge benefit by a factor of 3.83.
flags.action: Use C-LOWSPEED-CDIW-CURRENT. Cite C-LOWSPEED-CDI-CORRECTED-4CONCEPT only as history, with its supersession stated.

flags.title: Cruise dynamic pressure does not reconcile with the U values in our own report brief.
flags.detail: Liming Table 18 gives early cruise rho = 0.41271 kg/m3 and q_inf = 11258.7 Pa, which implies U = 233.580522 m/s. Our brief carries U = 233.934028 m/s, which with the same rho implies q = 11292.8041 Pa, a +0.303 % difference. Late cruise: Liming rho 0.31083, q 8232.4 implies U = 230.153066 m/s; our brief U = 230.466914 m/s implies q = 8254.8675 Pa, +0.273 %. The offset is consistent in sign and size, which points to a different assumed speed of sound rather than an arithmetic error.
flags.status: NOT RESOLVED HERE. Recorded, not adjudicated. It does not affect any dimensionless coefficient or any percentage, because VSPAERO is run in model units (Vinf = 100, rho = 0.002377) and the dimensional state is used only to set the target CL and to reconstruct aircraft-scale loads.
flags.action: Whoever writes the operating-point section should establish which speed of sound is authoritative before quoting a dimensional cruise load.

flags.title: The cruise aircraft-scale derivation and the low-speed coefficient normalisation are on different Sref, inside one report.
flags.detail: Cruise loads are reconstructed on Sref = 122.6 m2 with span 38.36 m, which preserves AR = 12 from the 12 ft2 basis. The low-speed coefficients are on 13.3572 ft2, AR 10.7807. Both appear in the same document without the difference being stated.
flags.action: Never place a cruise CDiw and a low-speed CDiw in one table without the Sref column.

flags.title: Claims with no operating point attached.
flags.detail: Two classes were found and both are qualitative, not numerical: (a) the Table 25 engineering decision matrix (outer mold line, load-shaping authority, maturity, gap/noise) carries no operating point because it carries no numbers; (b) the twist-axis travel figures ('reduces trailing-edge travel by approximately 10.7 %', 'doubles leading-edge travel') are GEOMETRIC ratios and are operating-point independent by construction.
flags.resolution: EVERY numerical performance claim extracted into this file has an operating_point id. None had to be recorded as unattached.

flags.detail: The 29 July report describes the 125-case database as 1 rigid + 40 conventional + 22 TE + 22 twist for the first 85-case pass plus 2 x 20 local refinements. The 19 August report, after 'provenance checks and deduplication', describes the same 125 evaluations as 1 rigid + 33 conventional + 51 TE + 40 twist. The total is 125 in both.
